M1.texto: In Huang et al. (ICLR 2024), intrinsic self-correction without oracle labels or tools did not improve reasoning and sometimes degraded it: GPT-4 on GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 (round 1) -> 89.0 (round 2); GPT-3.5 on CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8.

M2.texto: Self-Debugging with unit tests improves baseline accuracy by up to 12% on TransCoder and MBPP; GPT-4 without unit-test execution improves MBPP accuracy by only 3.6%.
M2.citacao_literal: On TransCoder and MBPP where unit tests are available, SELF-DEBUGGING improves the baseline accuracy by up to 12%.

M3.texto: In Reflexion, agent-generated internal tests had a 16.3% false-positive rate on MBPP Python versus 1.4% on HumanEval Python, and Reflexion's MBPP pass@1 (77.1) fell below the GPT-4 baseline (80.1).
M3.citacao_literal: the false positive test execution rate for MBPP Python is 16.3% while the rate for HumanEval Python is a mere 1.4%, leading to 91% overall accuracy

M4.texto: GPT-4 distinguishes its own summaries from those of two other LLMs and humans with 73.5% accuracy without fine-tuning, and self-preference correlates linearly with self-recognition when the fine-tuning task varies.
M4.citacao_literal: GPT-4 is 73.5% accurate distinguishing itself from two other LLMs and humans.

M5.texto: On leaderboard data (71 LLMs, 14,042 multiple-choice questions), pairs of models agree about 60% of the time when both err, and being from the same company adds only a few percentage points on top of that baseline.
M5.citacao_literal: We find substantial correlation in model errors—on one leaderboard dataset, models agree 60% of the time when both models err.

M9.texto: The verification-before-completion skill (obra/superpowers) states an evidence law and tells agents that when a delegated agent reports success they must check the VCS diff instead of trusting the report.
M9.citacao_literal: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE ... Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state

M10.texto: Anthropic's Claude Code best-practices guide warns that a reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some even when the work is sound, and recommends a fresh-context reviewer that sees only the diff and the criteria.
M10.citacao_literal: A reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some, even when the work is sound, because that is what it was asked to do.

M11.texto: In MT-Bench on 10 math questions (20 judgments with swapped positions), a GPT-4 judge with the default prompt declared incorrect answers correct in 70% of cases; showing the judge an independently generated reference answer cut that failure rate to 15%.
M11.citacao_literal: we first generate LLM judge’s answer independently, and then display it as a reference answer in the judge prompt. In Table 4, we see a significant improvement in failure rate (from 70% to 15%) over the default prompt.

M12.texto: Under a prompt that requires explanation and repair, LLMs falsely rejected correct code on average 54.8% (HumanEval) and 69.0% (MBPP) of the time; a fix-guided, execution-based verification filter lowered this to 16.3% and 28.9%.
M12.citacao_literal: Averaged across models, FNR drops from 54.8% to 16.3% on HumanEval and 69.0% to 28.9% on MBPP, while QuixBugs also improves (51.0% to 24.0%).

M13.texto: In LLM judges for code evaluation, a self-declared-correctness comment (for example 'correct code') was the most pronounced positive bias across all evaluated models and programming languages.
M13.citacao_literal: self-declared correctness exhibits the most pronounced effect across all evaluated models and programming languages

M14.texto: AOrchestra's context ablation on GAIA (50 samples): orchestrator-curated context for sub-agents scored 96.0, versus 86.0 with no context and 84.0 with full context.
M14.citacao_literal: whereas Full-Context often introduces irrelevant information and aggravates context degradation. In contrast, by allowing the orchestrator to select and compress only task-relevant history, our method provides a cleaner context and achieves the highest score.

M15.texto: Cognition reports that in a generator-verifier loop the review agent worked best when it shared no prior context with the coding agent, provided a communication bridge lets the main agent filter the reviewer's findings using its broader context.
M15.citacao_literal: Interestingly, we found this technique to work best when the coding and review agents do not share any context beforehand.
